question.text: Per the chapter, Enterprise Value (EV) is BEST described as:

answer.text: The market value of equity shares only
The debt-free/cash-free value of the operating business, representing total capital regardless of financing
Equity value plus all current liabilities
Book value of shareholders' funds only

explanation.text: The Logic: Quoted: 'Enterprise value (EV) is the debt-free/cash free value of the operating business... EV is the value of the total capital in the company or business regardless of whether it is debt or equity capital.' The Trap: Option A is Market Cap; Option C ignores the net-of-cash convention; Option D is book-based NAV. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XXI-B, XV and VIII all use EV as the standard entity value for multiples.
